agnostic_oa_obstruction_theory_transfer.interpretation: Source fact: the direct tangent-obstruction groups for pairs are Ext^i(I^bullet,F), while fixed-determinant complex deformations use trace-free Ext^{i+1}(I^bullet,I^bullet)_0. The source proves agreement not only at first order but over arbitrary nilpotent thickenings: it trims a deformed perfect complex, proves its cohomology has the needed purity and support, reconstructs it as {O -> F}, and proves F is flat. For the universal complex, rank one splits RHom into identity and trace-free summands; vanishing and Serre duality concentrate the trace-free part in degrees one and two, yielding a two-term perfect obstruction theory, virtual class, and deformation invariance. Inference: the useful change of representation is one that both preserves the moduli functor to all infinitesimal orders and exposes a removable scalar direction, shortening the remaining obstruction amplitude.

The Atiyah-class map (2.13), cited compatibility with obstruction classes, and Theorems 2.14-2.15 supply the perfect obstruction theory, virtual class, and relative deformation statement.

units.selection_reason: The direct deformation theory of pairs is not suitable for a virtual class, while the lossless fixed-determinant complex representation has trace-free deformation data. The source proves agreement of deformations to all nilpotent orders, reconstructs every fixed-determinant deformation as a pair, removes scalar directions by trace, and uses duality to concentrate the relevant complex in two degrees. The generic move is to transport a moduli problem to an equivalent representation where nuisance symmetries split off and obstruction amplitude becomes manageable.
